caption: A soccer ball rolled at a slant into a low garden wall bounces off at a slant the other way and rolls on across the lawn.

sa.check: A soccer ball rolls at a slant toward a low garden wall.
It rolls on across the lawn in a new direction.
The approach is at a slant rather than square to the wall.
The approach comes first and the bounce follows.

pc.expect: The ball leaves the wall on the opposite slant, turned away from the wall face, and rolls on a little slower than it arrived.
pc.fail: The ball comes straight back along the line it arrived on after a slanting approach; or it stops dead at the wall; or it leaves the wall quicker than it arrived.

pc.expect: The ball stays outside the wall and turns at its face.
pc.fail: The ball passes into the stone of the wall; or it sinks part way in before coming back out; or it passes through to the other side of the wall.

pc.expect: The change of direction happens where the ball meets the wall and nowhere else.
pc.fail: The ball turns away before it reaches the wall; or it turns again out on the open lawn with nothing touching it; or it stops and sets off again untouched.

pc.expect: The ball stays down on the grass, rolling rather than flying, through the bounce and afterwards.
pc.fail: The ball lifts off the lawn and travels through the air after the bounce; or it hovers above the grass; or it sinks into the lawn.

pc.expect: One ball and one wall are there throughout.
pc.fail: The ball vanishes at the wall or a second one appears; or the ball turns into another object at the bounce; or a section of the wall disappears where the ball strikes it.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The ball's panels, the wall and the garden stay the same.
pc.fail: The ball changes colour or pattern at the bounce; or the wall changes height between frames; or the garden behind rearranges.
